Queue::defined, Queue::dim, Queue::numel¶

Back to Queue API Reference

Signature¶

bool defined() const noexcept;
std::int64_t dim() const;
std::int64_t numel() const;

What It Does¶

These three forward directly to the held payload’s own defined(), dim(), and numel() – there is no Queue-specific shape or definedness concept layered on top. They work the same way regardless of which of the four kinds the Queue holds, which is the point: generic code can read a Queue’s shape without first checking kind().

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

defined() returns bool. dim() and numel() return std::int64_t, matching the held payload’s own rank and element count.

Examples¶

Example 1. A 1D Series-holding Queue.

pluss::Queue q(pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0}));
std::cout << "defined(): " << q.defined() << '\n';
std::cout << "dim(): " << q.dim() << '\n';
std::cout << "numel(): " << q.numel() << '\n';

Output¶

defined(): true
dim(): 1
numel(): 4

Example 2. A scalar Duration-holding Queue – dim() is 0, not 1, and numel() is 1 for a single scalar value, the same convention every PlussQit payload type uses for a 0D value.

pluss::Queue scalar_duration(pluss::duration::days(1));
std::cout << "duration dim(): " << scalar_duration.dim() << '\n';
std::cout << "duration numel(): " << scalar_duration.numel() << '\n';

Output¶

duration dim(): 0
duration numel(): 1

See Also¶

  • kind: identifying the payload these three describe.

  • accessors: getting the full payload back, not just its shape.
